page: Amazon Web Services is4gen.medium is a storage-optimized server instance powered by a single-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. Operating on the arm64 architecture at 2.5 GHz, this instance features one dedicated physical core and one thread. The hardware configuration includes 6.0 GB of system memory, providing a one-to-six ratio of vCPU to memory. It is equipped with 937 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, running on the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. While the stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls within the average category with a score of 1499.99, multi-core and memory-bound benchmarks are positioned in the lower percentiles. The Geekbench single-core score is 940.0, and the multi-core score is 938.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 59.32 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 19.51 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, both ranking in the bottom 10%. Cryptographic capabilities are supported via hardware AES, though advanced vector and matrix extensions are absent.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the is4gen.medium offers a high density of local NVMe SSD storage relative to its single-core compute allocation. This makes it a specialized option where storage capacity and local read/write speeds are prioritized over raw computational throughput or memory bandwidth. Given the 937 GB of NVMe SSD storage and 6.0 GB of RAM, this instance is suited for lightweight storage-intensive workloads, local caching, or small database operations that do not require high multi-threaded CPU performance.
